PREVIOUS NOTE, kept because a floor that loses its history costs more than the stamp gains:

core 1 -> 0. res.groups._compute_all_users_count was the whole core count: one search_count per group, over the group's all_implied_by_ids. It now fetches user_ids once for the implied groups of the whole recordset and takes len() of the union per group -- measured 2 queries for 13 groups where the loop cost 13.

THE ACTIVE_TEST SEMANTICS SURVIVE, and that is the reason the loop was written by hand in 4a6768ae1f6. all_users_count is compute_sudo and excludes archived users in a default context; _compute_all_user_ids fills the same x2many cache under active_test=False, which reads like a poisoning hazard. It is not one here: _RelationalMulti._get_read_context forces active_test off for the query that FILLS the cache and _make_corecords applies archived-ness on the way OUT, off the reading environment. So the cache is context-independent by construction and len() of a corecord set answers the reader's own active_test. Verified on a fresh base DB: old and new agree for every group, and agree again in all four cells of {default, active_test=False} x {user live, user archived}.

Scoped like the other per-addon gates: `addons` is the whole bundled tree as one number, and mail/account/stock/project each carry their own floor so a module cannot hide a regression inside the aggregate. Those four are untouched here.
